hooks.command: echo 'RE-GROUND FIRST: FROGS 5 Skyrim campaign. Before asserting any story fact or doing design work, read CLAUDE.md and Toryggs legacy/AI_README, then open the actual source (narrative chapters read IN ORDER are authoritative; trackers lag). Never state campaign canon from memory or the context summary.'

printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"PreToolUse","additionalContext":"CANON-WRITE CHECK: If this edits a source-of-truth doc (The Narrative/, world state tracking/, web/, Players/, Npcs/, factions/, Adventure modules/), verify every factual claim against source (cite chapter/line) before saving. Silent inaccuracies in canon are the worst failure mode."}}'

printf '%s' '{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"UserPromptSubmit","additionalContext":"GATES (every reply, no exceptions): G0 NO-SOURCE-NO-INVENT GATE (CLAUDE.md Rule 1, WRITING GUIDE Section XI) -- this campaign has a source of truth for nearly every possibility (geography, voice, mechanics, history, prior decisions). Creativity is licensed ONLY by a genuine, CHECKED absence of a source -- never by convenience. Before inventing any detail, check for it; if a reference (image, doc, prior message) already answered a question, re-open THAT, do not redraw/reimagine it. G1 CITATION GATE -- no canon claim, dialogue draft, or scene prose goes to the GM unless THIS message shows the source check first: file + line, QUOTED, not just claimed checked. G6 DIALOGUE GATE -- any line of dialogue for a named character needs an explicit pass/fail check against WRITING GUIDE Section IX rules 0-8, shown inline, before the line is presented -- INCLUDING Rule 8: no line may explain, in the same breath, why it is being said (no I will tell you X because Y self-justifying dialogue). G7 GATED-CLUE GATE (WRITING GUIDE Section X) -- any discoverable object placed behind a roll/difficulty must ship with its ACTUAL content in the same message (what it says, what it means, what a player can do with it) -- never a thematic image implying depth with nothing behind it; if the content is not ready, present the object as un-gated flavor instead, not as a check. Re-verify EVERY factual claim in a draft against source immediately before showing it -- a prior citation earlier in the conversation does not cover a new line written after it. Do not invent attributions, event order, or character reactions that are not directly sourced. G8 WHOLE-SCENE GATE -- before editing ANY part of a scene, RE-READ THE ENTIRE SCENE end to end THIS TURN (not the paragraph, not your own last draft, not recall -- recall decays silently and the draft still sounds confident) and state in one line that you re-read it and what it constrains. THE TELL YOU ARE IN VIOLATION: you are about to ask the GM a question about the scene -- almost every such question is already answered in the text, often in a line you wrote yourself. Go look before you ask. G9 ONE-CHANGE GATE -- a correction changes ONE thing; re-issue the previous text VERBATIM with only that change made. Do NOT rewrite around it (a fix on one axis silently breaks another and forces the GM to re-audit approved ground). And NEVER write a line that only parses against your own previous draft -- told it is too loud, DELETE the noise, do not add sentences reporting that things are quiet. The GM reads the current text cold; compensating lines are editing notes wearing prose. G10 GATES RUN BEFORE THE WRITING, NOT AFTER -- an audit appended to a finished draft catches formatting and launders the fabrication that already happened upstream. Order: open the sources, THEN draft against what they say, THEN show both. THE ROOT OF ALL OF THIS: the default move is to GENERATE something plausible where the correct move is to RETRIEVE what exists. The compendium exists so nothing ever has to be invented."}}'
